description:
FILED s470bs (Opus) from the filetest probe battery, which hit it by accident
once `-M *FH` started returning a real value.  PRE-EXISTING and INDEPENDENT of
that work: reproduces at 027ba9c, and under PCL_OPT=none, so it is not the
raw-slot emission.

MINIMAL REPRO (scratch/s470bs/p19.pl on the s470bs worktree):

    sub c { my $v = shift; return "EMPTY" if $v eq ''; return $v }
    my $q = eval "1/3";
    printf "03 [%-8s]\n", c($q);

  perl 5.40.3:  03 [0.333333333333333]
  PCL:          Unhandled type-error â¦ The value 0.3333333333333333
                is not of type SEQUENCE
                0: (PCL::SPRINTF-APPLY-WIDTH â¦)
                1: (PCL::SPRINTF-ONE â¦)

The whole program dies â nothing before the printf is even flushed.

THE MECHANISM, traced (`trace pcl::p-sprintf pcl::sprintf-one
pcl::sprintf-apply-width` on the emitted CL):

    1: (PCL::SPRINTF-ONE #\s "" NIL NIL
         (#S(P-BOX :VALUE 0.3333333333333333d0
                   :NV 0.3333333333333333d0 :NV-OK T
                   :SV 0.3333333333333333d0 :SV-OK T   <-- the SV cache is a DOUBLE
                   :CLASS NIL :IS-REF NIL)) 0)
      2: (PCL::SPRINTF-APPLY-WIDTH 0.3333333333333333d0 0 NIL NIL "")

`sprintf-one`'s %s arm does `(to-string val)`, which for a box is `box-sv`,
which returns the cached `sv` â and the cache holds a double, so
`(concatenate 'string sign-str str)` gets a non-sequence.  `stringify-value`
and `to-string` are BOTH correct in isolation (checked directly against the
core: `(to-string 1/3d0)` is "0.333333333333333").

TWO BUGS, one behind the other:

 (a) `%pcl-dualvar-p` FALSE-POSITIVES ON ORDINARY FLOATS.  Its test is

        (and (p-box-sv-ok v) (p-box-nv-ok v)
             (let ((n (to-number (p-box-sv v))))
               (and n (/= (p-box-nv v) n))))

     i.e. "the string half does not numify to the numeric half".  For a
     double, the sv cache holds perl's %.15g rendering, which round-trips to a
     DIFFERENT double for most values: 0.333333333333333 parses to
     0.333333333333333d0, not 0.3333333333333333d0.  So every float whose
     caches are both warm looks like a `$!`-style dualvar.  `$v eq ''` is
     what warms the sv cache, which is why the reproducer needs a string
     comparison in the sub.

 (b) `%p-dualvar-copy` COPIES THE WRONG SLOT.  It does
     `(setf (p-box-sv nb) s)` where `s` is `(p-box-value item)` â the box's
     RAW VALUE.  That is only the string half for a genuine `$!` dualvar,
     whose value IS the message; for anything else it writes a non-string into
     a slot every `to-string` reads.

FIX SHAPE (untried).  (b) alone removes the corruption and is a one-line,
obviously-correct change: copy `(p-box-sv item)`, the STRING cache, not the raw
value.  (a) is the real question and needs its own decision â the honest test
for "are these two halves inconsistent" is whether the sv cache is what
stringifying the nv would give, not whether numifying the sv gives the nv back.
Changing it also moves `Scalar::Util::isdual` and the raw-slot freeze decline
(`%pcl-raw-freeze-unsafe-p`), which share the predicate, so it wants a sweep.

NO ROW COST MEASURED â the gate, the sweep and the companion are all clean with
it, so nothing currently asserts the shape.  It is a whole-program crash on a
perfectly ordinary Perl idiom, which is why it is filed rather than left.
=== DONE (s473d) ===
SHIPPED as member 1 of s473d, commit "member 1 (#1230 + #1245): a dualvar is a
FACT of the representation, not an inference from the two caches" -- ONE cause
with #1245, so one commit.

WHAT IT WAS: %pcl-dualvar-p compared the two caches ("both valid and numifying
the string does not give the numeric"), and perl's %.15g rendering of a double
does not round-trip to the same double, so every cache-warm float looked like a
dualvar.  %p-dualvar-copy then wrote the box's RAW value into the STRING cache,
and the next reader that trusted sv-ok got a double where a string was promised.

THE FIX: a :DUAL marker on p-box's NV-OK (three-valued nil / t / :dual),
written only by p-errno-string, p-dualvar and the two dualvar copiers.
%p-dualvar-box-p DELETED (rule 11; its five call sites moved to the one
predicate); %p-dualvar-copy dies on a non-string (rule 12 at the WRITER, not a
coercion at each reader); the box-set carry-over and %p-container-snapshot
propagate the flag.

BARS: gate green (only the 13 pclxs xs rows); ir-conform 296 pass / 0 fail /
49 known / 0 stale, with 5 rows (335 337 338 342 343-string-eval) leaving
known-fail.tsv BY EDIT; probes identical to perl 5.40.3 under the default
emission AND PCL_OPT=none; guard Pl/t/numeric-repr-01.t rows A1-A3,
inverse-verified FAILING on a c4304834 git-archive extraction.  docs/ir-spec.md
gained section 3.2a (normative).  Final s473d tree: sweep TOTAL 18674 (+0),
GATE clean, drops 5 = census; gate 223 files / 7707 rows.
subject: CRASH (pre-existing, both emission paths): a box's STRING cache can be poisoned with a raw DOUBLE â `%pcl-dualvar-p` false-positives on ordinary floats, so `%p-leavesub-scalar` takes the dualvar branch and `%p-dualvar-copy` writes the box's raw VALUE into the sv slot.  `printf "%s"` then dies "The value 0.333â¦ is not of type SEQUENCE" and the whole program is lost.
